observations.title: Pathogen contamination in finished pet food
observations.summary: State and FDA testing found Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes, and Campylobacter jejuni in multiple pet food lots, rendering the products adulterated because they contain harmful pathogens.

observations.title: Aerosolized water and contaminated totes during production
observations.summary: Investigator observed a high‑pressure water hose cleaning a shovel, causing overspray that contacted uncovered finished product, and cracked, uncleaned plastic totes exposing in‑process food to floor contaminants.

observations.title: Rusty equipment and harborage sites
observations.summary: Investigator observed rust on food‑contact surfaces of grinders, chutes, and a pitchfork, providing harborage areas for pathogens in the manufacturing environment.

observations.title: Improper temperature control during distribution
observations.summary: Finished frozen pet food was shipped in unrefrigerated trucks without controls to maintain appropriate time‑and‑temperature conditions, allowing potential pathogen growth during transport.
